claim_restated: Pan-cancer, tumors with a pathogenic/likely-pathogenic germline predisposition variant (in genes incl. BRCA1) show loss of heterozygosity or a biallelic two-hit event at that locus in this fraction of cases
source_population: 677 predisposition-variant-bearing tumors (659 SNV/indel + 18 large deletions) across 33 TCGA cancer types, n=10389 adult cancers total cohort
citation: Huang KL et al. "Pathogenic Germline Variants in 10,389 Adult Cancers." Cell. 2018 Apr 5;173(2):355-370.e14.
applies_to_design_note: Pan-cancer ceiling for expected LOH/two-hit rate; our design's per-carrier LOH rate should not be interpreted against this alone without the breast-specific, gene-stratified numbers in LOH02.

claim_restated: In germline BRCA1 carriers' breast tumors, locus-specific LOH (loss of the wild-type allele) is present in this fraction; in germline BRCA2 carriers' breast tumors, in this fraction
source_population: 160 germline BRCA1/BRCA2-associated breast and ovarian tumors (retention of wild-type allele reported in 10% of BRCA1 breast, 46% of BRCA2 breast, 7% of BRCA1 ovarian, 16% of BRCA2 ovarian tumors; LOH = complement)
citation: Maxwell KN et al. "BRCA locus-specific loss of heterozygosity in germline BRCA1 and BRCA2 carriers." Nat Commun. 2017 Aug 22;8:319.
applies_to_design_note: Primary, gene- and tissue-stratified LOH benchmark for our breast-cancer design; BRCA2 breast LOH (54%) is materially lower than BRCA1 breast (90%) and should not be pooled.

claim_restated: In high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma overall (not stratified by BRCA status), the homologous-recombination pathway is estimated defective/deficient in about this fraction of tumors
citation: The Cancer Genome Atlas Research Network. "Integrated genomic analyses of ovarian carcinoma." Nature. 2011 Jun 30;474(7353):609-615.
applies_to_design_note: Foundational, unstratified HRD prevalence estimate for HGSOC; establishes the ~50% baseline our design's expected HRD-high proportion should be compared against, but is not BRCA-mutant-vs-wild-type stratified (see HRD02, NF01).

claim_restated: A combined DNA-based HRD score (unweighted sum of LOH, TAI, and LST components) is correlated with BRCA1/2 defects across breast cancer subtypes, providing the analytic basis subsequently used to define an HRD-positive threshold
value: correlation established (no single percent reported for this claim)
source_population: 215 breast tumors across all ER/HER2 subtypes, commercial specimens
citation: Timms KM et al. "Association of BRCA1/2 defects with genomic scores predictive of DNA damage repair deficiency among breast cancer subtypes." Breast Cancer Res. 2014 Dec 5;16(6):475.
applies_to_design_note: Methodological basis for the composite HRD (LOH+TAI+LST) score our design would compute; precedes and underlies the GIS>=42 threshold in HRD03.

claim_restated: The established genomic-instability-score (GIS) threshold for HRD-positive status is this value; it was used to define HR-deficiency (score >=42, or a BRCA1/2 mutation) and shown to predict pathologic response to platinum-based neoadjuvant chemotherapy in triple-negative breast cancer
source_population: 267 TNBC patients pooled across 3 neoadjuvant platinum trials incl. PrECOG 0105 (n=72)
citation: Telli ML et al. "Homologous Recombination Deficiency (HRD) Score Predicts Response to Platinum-Containing Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy in Patients with Triple-Negative Breast Cancer." Clin Cancer Res. 2016 Aug 1;22(15):3764-73.
applies_to_design_note: This is the specific GIS>=42 cutoff our design should use if adopting the Myriad myChoice-style composite score; clinical-benefit validation (not just biomarker-response) is in HRD04.

claim_restated: Clinical (treatment-benefit) validation of the GIS threshold: adding olaparib to bevacizumab maintenance produced a progression-free-survival benefit in newly diagnosed advanced ovarian cancer, concentrated in the HRD-positive (BRCA-mutant and/or GIS>=42) subgroup
citation: Ray-Coquard I et al. "Olaparib plus Bevacizumab as First-Line Maintenance in Ovarian Cancer." N Engl J Med. 2019.
applies_to_design_note: Establishes that the GIS>=42 threshold (HRD03) has clinical-outcome validation, not just biomarker correlation -- the relevant citation if our design frames HRD-high status as clinically actionable.

claim_restated: HGSOC HRD-high proportion stratified by BRCA1/2 mutation status (BRCA-mutant % vs BRCA-wild-type %), from a single primary source with a confirmed resolving URL
applies_to_design_note: An earlier search surfaced "228/352 (65%) HRD-positive: 102 (29%) BRCA-mutant, 126 (36%) BRCA-wild-type" as search-summary prose only, with no specific backing link found on follow-up -- excluded per Standing Rule 3 (no URL, don't assert). See BENCHMARKS_NOTES.md. The unstratified ~50% HGSOC estimate (HRD01) remains available; any control needing the BRCA-stratified split cannot run yet.

claim_restated: A published, array/exome-derived HRD score (LOH + TAI + LST composite) plus a broader DNA-damage-repair (DDR) deficiency score set was computed pan-cancer across TCGA and made available as a supplementary dataset
value: computed for 8464 tumor samples across 33 cancer types
citation: Knijnenburg TA et al. "Genomic and Molecular Landscape of DNA Damage Repair Deficiency across The Cancer Genome Atlas." Cell Rep. 2018 Apr 3;23(1):239-254.e6.
applies_to_design_note: This is the dataset our design would use as the published TCGA array-derived HRD/DDR score reference. The paper's existence, scope (8464 samples) and DOI are confirmed; the exact current download location for the underlying per-sample score table is NOT confirmed this session (see DDR02).

claim_restated: Direct, currently-live download URL/Synapse ID for the Knijnenburg et al. (DDR01) per-sample HRD/DDR score table
applies_to_design_note: cell.com (the paper itself) is not fetchable in this session (WebFetch to cell.com and to synapse.org both blocked by this environment's network policy -- see BENCHMARKS_NOTES.md); WebSearch did not surface a specific, currently-resolving Synapse/data-portal ID. Do not invent one (Standing Rule 3). A future session with unblocked egress to synapse.org / cell.com should resolve this before the corresponding control is built.

claim_restated: TCGA breast cancer: only TP53, PIK3CA, and GATA3 are somatically mutated at >10% incidence across the whole cohort (unstratified single-percent values for TP53/PIK3CA are NOT independently confirmed this session -- see TP02 for a numeric estimate from a secondary TCGA analysis)
citation: The Cancer Genome Atlas Network. "Comprehensive molecular portraits of human breast tumours." Nature. 2012 Oct 4;490(7418):61-70.
applies_to_design_note: Primary TCGA-BRCA source; nature.com is not directly fetchable in this session (blocked, see notes) so this row reports only the >10% threshold claim that surfaced via search, not an exact overall TP53/PIK3CA percentage from the primary paper itself -- do not treat TP02's numbers as if they were read directly from this paper.

claim_restated: In a next-generation-sequencing analysis of the TCGA invasive breast carcinoma cohort, TP53 was somatically mutated in this fraction of tumors and PIK3CA in this fraction
citation: A microscopic landscape of the invasive breast cancer genome. Sci Rep. 2016.
applies_to_design_note: Numeric TP53/PIK3CA frequency benchmark for our TCGA-BRCA somatic-mutation control; note this is a secondary analysis of a 680-case IDC subset, not the full 825-tumor primary TCGA cohort in TP01 -- listed separately per instruction not to merge sources.

claim_restated: TCGA breast cancer PAM50 intrinsic-subtype counts (mRNA-subtyped subset): Luminal A, Luminal B, HER2-enriched, Basal-like
source_population: 501 mRNA-subtyped tumors (of the 825-tumor primary TCGA-BRCA cohort; Figure 1 of the primary paper)
citation: The Cancer Genome Atlas Network. "Comprehensive molecular portraits of human breast tumours." Nature. 2012 Oct 4;490(7418):61-70.
applies_to_design_note: Computed proportions (of 501): LumA 44.9%, LumB 25.1%, HER2E 11.4%, Basal 18.6%. Counts surfaced via WebSearch synthesis of the primary paper's Figure 1, not independently read from the paper directly (nature.com blocked this session, see notes) -- treat the percentages as approximate pending direct-fetch confirmation. Excludes a small Normal-like group not captured in this search.

claim_restated: ENIGMA/BCAC/CIMBA tumor-pathology likelihood ratio for BRCA1 mutation status: ER-negative, grade 3 breast cancer pathology, stratified by age at diagnosis
source_population: Large-scale pooled analysis, BCAC + CIMBA + ENIGMA consortia (multi-thousand case-control breast cancer pathology dataset)
citation: Spurdle AB et al. "Refined histopathological predictors of BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutation status: a large-scale analysis of breast cancer characteristics from the BCAC, CIMBA, and ENIGMA consortia." Breast Cancer Res. 2014 Dec 23;16(6):3419.
applies_to_design_note: Primary source for the tumor-pathology likelihood-ratio component (PP4-type evidence) our design would use for BRCA1 germline VUS classification.

claim_restated: Same source, BRCA2 mutation status: ER-positive grade 3 pathology (irrespective of age), and ER-negative grade 3 pathology at age>=50
value: LR ~1.7 (ER+ grade 3, any age); LR 1.54 (95% CI 1.27-1.88) (ER- grade 3, age>=50)
citation: Spurdle AB et al., Breast Cancer Res. 2014 Dec 23;16(6):3419.
applies_to_design_note: BRCA2 pathology LRs are much weaker than BRCA1's (contrast with ENIGMA01) -- our design must not apply one gene's LR table to the other.

claim_restated: Bayesian ACMG/AMP framework: OddsPath thresholds separating supporting / moderate / strong / very strong evidence toward pathogenicity
source_population: n/a (statistical/methodological framework, not a patient cohort)
citation: Tavtigian SV et al. "Modeling the ACMG/AMP variant classification guidelines as a Bayesian classification framework." Genet Med. 2018 Sep;20(9):1054-1060.
applies_to_design_note: These are the exact OddsPath cut-points our design must use to convert any quantitative evidence (e.g. functional-assay or co-segregation data) into ACMG evidence strength; benign-direction thresholds are the reciprocals (ODDS02).

citation: Tavtigian SV et al., Genet Med. 2018 Sep;20(9):1054-1060.
applies_to_design_note: Computed as reciprocals of ODDS01's pathogenic thresholds per the paper's stated symmetric Bayesian framework; not independently re-derived from a directly-fetched copy of the paper this session (gimjournal.org / sciencedirect.com not confirmed fetchable -- see notes), so treat the exact reciprocal values as consistent-with, not independently verified against, the primary text.
